subject: Re: Redwood vs Hyperscaler inference incident response & SLAs
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Liz Jenkins <liz.jenkins@acme.com>, ACME SRE Team <sre@acme.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood follow-up: incident response expectations & next tests

Hi Liz / SRE team -

Thanks again for taking the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: \n
- What we heard: Acme's top priorities for inference reliability are (1) predictable latencies under traffic spikes, (2) a clear incident response timeline and RCA cadence, and (3) guaranteed log/audit access for post-incident analysis.
- Where Redwood fits: we discussed our unified runtime + routing fallbacks, SLA tiers (99.9% vs 99.95% for Dedicated), and our standard incident response commitments (P1 ack < 15 min, escalations to on-call engineer within 30 min).
- Immediate asks from Acme: a comparison of our incident response + escalation process vs. hyperscalers (AWS/Azure) and how we handle RCA ownership for model-serving incidents; also a short joint runbook for a simulated outage test.

Attachments: draft SLA compare (PDF) and incident response runbook (DOCX) - see attached.

Proposed next steps: \n1) Redwood to share a concise SLA/incident comparison and a one-page runbook for the simulation (I attached drafts).
2) Acme to confirm a 2-hour window for a simulation next week (ideally Wed 7/22 afternoon PST).
3) If agreeable, we'll schedule a follow-up where our SRE (Vivek) walks through the runbook and escalation tree with your on-call.

If anything above is off, say so - otherwise I'll plan to send a formal comparison doc and calendar invite.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0132

Attachments: redwood-hyperscaler-sla-compare.pdf (14KB), incident-response-runbook.docx (23KB)

From: Liz Jenkins <liz.jenkins@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 08:50:13 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood follow-up: incident response expectations & next tests

Thanks Marissa - this looks good. A couple of clarifications from our side: \n
- For RCAs: Our security/compliance team wants a commitment that RCAs include (a) timeline of events, (b) root cause analysis that specifies whether the issue was infra/model/config, and (c) remedial action and owners. Hyperscalers typically provide an RCA but push some of the investigation back to the customer; we need to understand how Redwood supports the investigation for model-serving issues.
- Simulation window: Wed 7/22 between 1-4pm PST works for our on-call. Prefer 2pm if possible.

Can Vivek join the runbook walkthrough? Also, can you flag any differences in RCA depth between Redwood Dedicated and Hosted API?

Liz
Liz Jenkins
Director, Platform Reliability | Acme Corp
liz.jenkins@acme.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Liz Jenkins <liz.jenkins@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 10:05:42 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood follow-up: incident response expectations & next tests

Thanks, Liz - quick note from the engineering side. I attached a short SLA/incident comparison table that highlights the differences vs AWS/Azure for servable endpoints. Highlights: \n
- RCA ownership: For Dedicated customers, Redwood provides full-run RCAs (we lead the investigation, provide logs + analyzed timelines, and propose remediation with owners). For Hosted customers we provide the same artifacts but the scope of investigation for customer-managed models is collaborative; we define the investigation boundaries in the MSA.
- P1 timelines: Redwood standard: ack < 15m, initial triage update < 1h, full RCA draft within 72h for Dedicated (extended if deep forensic needed). Hyperscalers: variable - generally ack within 1h and RCA often provided as a summary after 3-7 days depending on impact.
- Escalation: We have a two-tier on-call with SRE + customer success; Dedicated contracts include a named escalation path and periodic incident postmortems.

Proposed tests for the simulation: \n1) Injected latency spike under 100 RPS sustained for 10 minutes - validate routing fallback to lower-cost variant and observe latency tail.
2) KV cache eviction scenario - observe warm-up behavior and recovery time.
3) Full node outage where we trigger failover to different capacity pool.

I can run through the runbook at 2pm PST on Wed. Attaching: redwood-hyperscaler-sla-compare.pdf (concise) and incident-response-runbook.docx (v0.3).

--Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Redwood follow-up: incident response expectations & next tests

Liz - great, confirming simulation for Wed 2026-07-22 at 14:00 PST. Calendar invite sent.

Quick notes on what we'll deliver during the simulation: \n- Live walkthrough of the runbook and escalation phone bridge.
- Execution of the first two simulation tests (latency spike + KV eviction). If time permits we'll trigger the failover scenario.
- Post-sim output: timeline, captured logs (obfuscated as needed), and a draft RCA within 72h. For Dedicated customers we commit to leading the RCA and naming remediation owners.

Action items: \n- Acme: confirm list of on-call participants and any blast radius constraints for the tests.
- Redwood (Rishi/Vivek): bring runbook, monitoring dashboards, and a pre-seeded log bundle for quicker analysis.

Thanks - looking forward to it.
Marissa
